title: BSP Consumer Expectations Survey Q4 2025 (public source)
summary: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas' quarterly survey of household sentiment on the economy, family finances, saving, borrowing and the use of overseas remittances.
label_notes: Pages are 1-based PDF page indexes. Confidence, saving-intention and borrowing-intention indices are diffusion indices (share of optimists minus pessimists), recorded with unit 'score' because they are not shares of respondents.

findings.text: Household confidence fell in Q4 2025: the overall current-quarter confidence index dropped from -9.8 in Q3 2025 to -22.2.
findings.quote: overall current-quarter confidence index (CI) turned more negative from -9.8 percent in Q3 2025 to -22.2 percent in Q4 2025

findings.text: Households linked the weaker confidence mainly to graft and corruption in government, higher inflation, lower household income and bad weather.
findings.quote: mainly due to concerns over: (a) graft and corruption in the government, (b) higher inflation, (c) lower household income, and (d) unfavorable weather conditions

findings.text: The saving intention index turned positive, from -8.8 in Q3 2025 to 4.6 in Q4 2025.
findings.quote: saving intention index reverted to positive territory from -8.8 percent in Q3 2025 to 4.6 percent in Q4 2025

findings.text: Among households planning to save, 29.7% intended to set aside at least 10% of monthly gross family income, up from 23.9% in Q3 2025.
findings.quote: set aside at least 10 percent of their monthly gross family income rose from 23.9 percent in Q3 2025 to 29.7 percent in Q4 2025

findings.text: Of households receiving overseas remittances, 36.4% put part of them into savings and 29.0% used them for debt payments.
findings.quote: remittances to education (63.9 percent) and savings (36.4 percent) declined

findings.text: Borrowing intentions stayed deeply negative: the borrowing intention index for the next quarter was -71.7 (from -74.1 in Q3 2025).
findings.quote: turned less negative from -74.1 percent and -66.2 percent in the Q3 2025 survey to -71.7 percent and -64.5 percent
